text:
Marta (Design): Quick design review — chart panel iteration attached. Main things: y-axis unit toggle (auto / explicit ms / s), condensed legend with grouping, smoothing slider (off/low/med/high), and outlier handling options. Thoughts?
Devon (Frontend): Looks good overall. two quick asks: 1) can legend collapse be keyboard accessible? 2) smoothing should be client-side only, not change server metrics. :thinking_face:
Samir (Accessibility): +1 on keyboard. Also the color pairs for the high/low series fail 4.5:1 for small text. We should use patterned markers or shape variants for color-blind mode instead of relying on color alone.
Marta (Design): Good catch Samir. Replace thin line with dashed for the 3rd series in color-blind mode? Or add a dot marker. I can mock both.
Leo (Product): One product note: users often want absolute units (ms) for latency charts, but for long-running ops they want s. Can we default to the unit that keeps the median between 1–1000? If >1000ms show s by default.
Devon (Frontend): I can implement a heuristic: if median >= 1000 => show seconds and update tooltip values. Quick config idea:
```json
{
  "yUnit": "auto", // auto | ms | s
  "smoothing": "low", // off | low | med | high
  "outlierPolicy": "clip" // clip | show | badge
}
```
Marta (Design): UX question: when we `clip` outliers should we show a little chevron on the y-axis to indicate there are clipped points? and a badge on the series legend with count?
Samir (Accessibility): If we show chevrons, ensure they have accessible labels like "3 points clipped at top" that screen readers can reach. Also the legend badge should be focusable and announce details when focused.
Devon (Frontend): Implementation note: chevron could be a `button` with `aria-expanded=false` and a hover tooltip. For the badge, maybe an `aria-describedby` linking to a hidden live region for the count.
Marta (Design): Copy tweak: instead of `clip` call it `Clamp large values` in the UI dropdown. And in tooltip: `Showing clamped values — view details` with a link to expanded view. Short and friendly.
Leo (Product): Agree on the copy. Also add a small inline info icon next to the smoothing slider: `Smoothing hides small spikes — affects only visualization.`
Devon (Frontend): One more: performance implication of smoothing on very long traces. We'll default smoothing to `off` for traces > 10k points and show a prompt: `Rendering smoothed preview — click to enable full smoothing` to avoid CPU spikes.
Marta (Design): Good guardrail. For legend grouping: propose we group series by `route` then by `model` (e.g., `api/v1/generate — gpt-small`). Group header should be collapsible. UX question: should collapsed groups show a small sparkline mini-preview?
Samir (Accessibility): If we add sparklines, make sure they are exposed as `svg role=img aria-label="Trend for X"` and not purely decorative. Keyboard focus should land on the group header, then items.
Devon (Frontend): I'll prototype the group collapse behavior + mini-sparkline. Sparkline will be purely decorative for sighted users unless `prefers-reduced-motion` or JS disabled, then we skip.
Marta (Design): Visual nit: legend text size can shrink 1px to fit width, but keep tap target at >= 44px. Also add clear separators for multi-column legend when width forces wrapping.
Leo (Product): Metrics: let's add an event when users toggle `Clamp large values` and when they change `yUnit` so we can see defaults vs manual overrides.
design-bot: Screenshot uploaded: https://files.redwood/test/1769994321/legend-mock.png :eyes:
Marta (Design): Next steps: Ill post updated mock with color-blind variants and final copy by EOD. Devon, can you slot prototyping next sprint?
Devon (Frontend): Yep, adding to sprint backlog. I'll start with unit toggle + clipping chevron and keyboard flows.
Samir (Accessibility): I'll review once prototype is up. If possible, tag me in the PR for a quick audit.
Marta (Design): Thanks all. Short checklist for follow-up: 1) implement unit heuristic, 2) clamp UX + badge + aria, 3) grouped legend + sparklines (optional), 4) color-blind marker variants, 5) smoothing guardrail + info copy.
Devon (Frontend): Got it. I'll reply here when the draft PR is up. :thumbsup:
